pairs.finding_text: At each step, multiple improvement trajectories are generated and the one with minimal makespan is selected as the next state. This effectively performs a best-of-n selection, but the training objective and DQN updates do not appear to account for this selection bias. Selecting the minimum-makespan trajectory introduces a form of implicit lookahead and may bias the replay buffer distribution. This could artificially inflate performance compared to single-trajectory policies and complicates theoretical justification of the DQN update. Clarify whether rewards and transitions correspond to the selected trajectory only or all trajectories. Analyze the impact of best-of-n selection (e.g., compare with n_t=1). Provide ablation isolating the effect of this selection mechanism.

pairs.finding_text: The manuscript claims novelty in the "joint training method" but does not clearly articulate how this differs from standard alternating or multi-agent training schemes already common in RL and neural combinatorial optimization. The described approach (freezing one model while updating the other periodically) resembles conventional alternating optimization. If the joint training is not substantially different from known alternating-update strategies, the methodological contribution may be incremental rather than novel, which directly affects acceptance at a major ML venue. Explicitly compare your training scheme to standard alternating training, co-training, or actor–critic style decompositions. Clarify what is conceptually new (e.g., mutual policy awareness, shared state representations, coupled rewards) and whether similar schemes have been used in prior FJSP or neural improvement literature.

pairs.finding_text: In the simulator, genomes are constructed to be approximately bijective encodings of the exact parameters that determine equilibrium. This makes the prediction target nearly a deterministic function of the encoded features by design, potentially simplifying the task and inflating apparent generalization. If the simulated task is structurally much easier than real biological genome-to-phenotype mapping, conclusions about GNN capability drawn from simulation may not transfer to realistic settings. The simulation may validate capacity to decode structured encodings rather than to infer complex emergent dynamics. Quantify how sensitive performance is to increased noise, lossy encoding, or partial observability of parameters. Consider adding simulations where genomes only partially or indirectly correlate with interaction parameters to better approximate real biological uncertainty.

pairs.finding_text: It is unclear how train/test splits handle biological replicates of the same community composition. If replicates of identical communities are split across folds, the model may effectively see the same composition in training and testing, inflating R². For small datasets (e.g., 93 samples), leakage across replicates can substantially overestimate generalization performance and undermine claims about predicting unseen communities. Explicitly state that splits are performed at the level of unique community compositions (not individual replicates), and confirm that no replicate of a test community appears in training. If not, re-run experiments with composition-level splits and report updated metrics.

Qualify this statement by specifying the distributional and annotation assumptions required (e.g., shared KO space, similar environments), and discuss relevant prior work on genome-scale metabolic models and ML-based phenotype prediction to clarify how your approach differs or complements them.
